blocks.text: Abbotsford Condos Under $800K: streets and boundaries

items.t: The core the condos cluster in is planned, not accidental: the City Centre Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw 2913-2019) and the Historic Downtown Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw 2920-2019) are adopted neighbourhood plans under the city-wide Abbotsforward 2050 Official Community Plan (OCP), and they cover the Mill Lake, South Fraser Way and Historic Downtown ground where apartment buildings stand.

blocks.text: Abbotsford Condos Under $800K: the housing stock

items.t: Abbotsford's tallest condo stock is one named tower: Mahogany at Mill Lake, 2180 Gladwin Road — a 27-storey concrete residential tower with 152 suites above three storeys of commercial space and a two-level underground parkade, developed by Quantum Properties Mahogany LP and built by Ventana Construction.

Part of that tower is not strata resale stock at all: floors five through ten of Mahogany are operated by Aging in Place at Mahogany as private, full-sized rental suites for independent senior living — six floor plans from 674 to 1,661 square feet — so a buyer searching the building will meet both strata units and rental suites at the same address.

The low-rise end of the stock is planned at six storeys and under: the Historic Downtown plan's Urban 1 – Midrise designation allows up to 6 storeys, and its Urban 2 – Ground Oriented designation enables rowhouses, townhouse, multiplex or duplex housing.

Abbotsford condos are freehold strata, and the provincial strata framework — depreciation reports, strata records and the Form B information certificate — is the document set that describes any specific building in this band.

blocks.text: Abbotsford Condos Under $800K: rules that affect buyers

items.t: New condo form in the core is set by the two adopted neighbourhood plans: the City Centre plan (Bylaw 2913-2019) and Historic Downtown plan (Bylaw 2920-2019) designations decide where midrise and mixed-use buildings can go, under the Abbotsforward 2050 OCP.

One utility rule splits Abbotsford condo addresses in two: water and sewer customers are billed bi-monthly, except customers in the Clearbrook Waterworks District, who are billed quarterly for sewer services — two buildings in this band can be on different City billing cycles.

blocks.text: Abbotsford Condos Under $800K: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Abbotsford gives a 5 percent discount on the utility bill if payment is received by the due date printed on the bill — a small, automatic saving that only exists if the bill is paid on time.

Any utility account balance still outstanding at December 31 is transferred to the property tax account and charged daily interest, so a condo seller's unpaid City utility bill becomes a tax-account problem for the property.
Mill Lake Park, the green edge of the central condo stock, is accessed from Bevan Avenue and Emerson Street.

Bourquin Exchange is the central transit exchange, and BC Transit's Central Fraser Valley network names routes 1 (Highstreet/UFV), 2 (Highstreet/McMillan), 5 (Clearbrook/Bourquin via Hospital), 12 (UFV/Bourquin) and 21 (Aldergrove/Abbotsford) among the services tying the condo core to the University of the Fraser Valley (UFV), the hospital and Highstreet.

Abbotsford Regional Hospital and Cancer Centre is at 32900 Marshall Road, and the Abbotsford Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at Unit 100, 2692 Clearbrook Road — the two Fraser Health anchors at either end of the central condo corridor.
Clearbrook Library is at 32320 George Ferguson Way and the Abbotsford branch library is at 33355 Bevan Avenue, both inside the central area the condo stock sits in.

blocks.text: Abbotsford Condos Under $800K: development and new projects

items.t: Montvue, Historic Downtown — two 5-storey mixed-use buildings by Parcel7 Homes, with 90 homes above ground-floor commercial space; status: completed 2025, per the project architect's page (as of November 3, 2026) — the newest completed low-rise condo form in the downtown core.

City Centre and Historic Downtown neighbourhood plans — adopted plans (Bylaws 2913-2019 and 2920-2019) that set the midrise and mixed-use designations the next core condo buildings will be approved under; status: adopted, under the Abbotsforward 2050 OCP (as of November 3, 2026).

blocks.text: Abbotsford Condos Under $800K: costs and taxes

items.t: The condo-relevant City charges are metered utilities: residential water at $1.46 per cubic metre and sewer at $1.35 per cubic metre, effective March 1, 2026, billed bi-monthly (quarterly for sewer in the Clearbrook Waterworks District), with a 5 percent discount for payment by the due date.

Abbotsford has no SkyTrain; the condo core runs on BC Transit buses through Bourquin Exchange, including route 1 (Highstreet/UFV), route 2 (Highstreet/McMillan), route 5 (Clearbrook/Bourquin via Hospital), route 12 (UFV/Bourquin) and route 31 (Abbotsford/Mission).
South Fraser Way is the commercial backbone of the City Centre, and Highway 1 interchanges at McCallum Road and Clearbrook Road serve the central condo area, with Highway 11 running north to Mission.
The OCP designates South Fraser Way between Clearbrook and McCallum Road as a Primary Transit Corridor — the planning commitment behind bus priority on the street most central condos front.

blocks.text: Abbotsford Condos Under $800K: risks and due diligence

items.t: Read the depreciation report and contingency reserve position before subject removal: Fraser Valley stratas had a July 1, 2026 deadline for a current report, and a building that just commissioned its first report in years is a building whose levy schedule is about to be written.

Confirm the tenure of the specific suite in a mixed building: at Mahogany at Mill Lake, floors five through ten are operator-run rental suites, not strata lots, so a "unit in the tower" is not automatically a strata purchase.

British Columbia strata disputes can be resolved through the Civil Resolution Tribunal, and the Province's strata housing pages set out how strata ownership, records and dispute resolution work — the official route if a records dispute follows a purchase.

faq.q: As a first-time buyer, does the property transfer tax (PTT) exemption reach condos in this band?
faq.a: Because this page's band caps at $800,000, a qualifying first-time buyer anywhere in the band is under the full-exemption value ceiling — confirm eligibility with a legal professional before writing.

faq.q: What is unusual about the Mahogany at Mill Lake tower?
faq.a: Two things a buyer would not expect. It is a 27-storey concrete tower of 152 suites at 2180 Gladwin Road, developed by Quantum Properties Mahogany LP, standing above three storeys of commercial space beside Mill Lake. And floors five through ten are not strata lots for sale — the building's own operator runs them as private rental suites for independent senior living, in six floor plans from 674 to 1,661 square feet. Check which tenure a specific suite is before comparing it to strata resales in the same building.

faq.q: How does the City bill a condo for water and sewer?
faq.a: By metered consumption, billed bi-monthly for most of the city: effective March 1, 2026, the residential water rate is $1.46 per cubic metre and the sewer rate is $1.35 per cubic metre, after Council approved a 4 percent increase to both in January 2026. Paying by the due date printed on the bill earns a 5 percent discount. The exception is the Clearbrook Waterworks District, where sewer is billed quarterly — so the building's district, not just its strata fees, decides the utility rhythm a buyer inherits.

faq.q: Which schools serve a Central Abbotsford condo?
faq.a: School District 34 catchments are address-based and set through the district's School Locator portal for the primary home address. A condo building's own address must be run before any school is marketed with the unit.

faq.q: Does the $800K cap cover the typical Abbotsford condo?
faq.a: The cap sits above the middle of the combined attached market: the Abbotsford Condos & Townhomes median sale price was $497,500 in September 2026 — $302,500 below the cap — though that median mixes townhomes with condos, so treat it as context for where the cap sits, not as the price of a typical condo (SnapStats, September 2026)

faq.q: Where does Abbotsford's attached stock actually sit?
faq.a: By September 2026 inventory, Central Abbotsford held 256 Condos & Townhomes listings and Abbotsford West 210, out of 572 Abbotsford-wide, and the rural sub-areas (Bradner, Matsqui, Sumas Mountain, Sumas Prairie) held none — those are combined condo-and-townhome inventory counts, not counts of condos under the cap (SnapStats, September 2026)

faq.q: Can a first-time buyer use the PTT exemption under $800K in Abbotsford?
faq.a: In principle, yes — the first time home buyers' program's full exemption runs to a fair market value of $835,000 (exempting the first $500,000 of price), with a partial exemption to $860,000, provided the buyer meets all the program's personal and property conditions; the exemption is claimed through the buyer's legal professional on the PTT return.
